module_title: Buddhism and Jainism - Literature, Sects, and Expansion
introduction: With the expansion of Buddhism and Jainism, their literature, sects, and organizational structures also developed. At this level, we will understand their scriptures, divisions, and methods of spread, which are frequently asked in exams.

core_concepts.title: Buddhist Literature (Tripitaka)
core_concepts.description: The primary literature of Buddhism is the Tripitaka, which includes the Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, and Abhidhamma Pitaka. These contain the teachings of Buddha and the rules of the Sangha.

core_concepts.title: Buddhist Sects
core_concepts.description: Buddhism was mainly divided into two sects - Hinayana and Mahayana. Hinayana considers Buddha as a human teacher, whereas Mahayana worships him as a divine figure.

core_concepts.title: Jain Literature
core_concepts.description: The main texts of Jainism are the Agamas, which are based on the teachings of Mahavira. These were written in the Prakrit language.

core_concepts.title: Jain Sects
core_concepts.description: Jainism is divided into two main sects - Digambara and Svetambara. Digambara emphasizes nudity and strict asceticism, while Svetambara followers wear white clothes.

core_concepts.title: Spread of Religions
core_concepts.description: Buddhism spread widely under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka and reached Sri Lanka, China, and Japan. Jainism mainly spread in the western and southern parts of India.

important_entities.name: Tripitaka
important_entities.significance: Compilation of Buddha’s teachings and monastic rules

important_entities.name: Hinayana
important_entities.significance: Considers Buddha as a human and rejects idol worship

important_entities.name: Mahayana
important_entities.significance: Accepts worship of Buddha and the concept of Bodhisattva

important_entities.name: Svetambara
important_entities.significance: Followers wear white clothes and follow a relatively liberal approach

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mix them up: Hinayana does not consider Buddha as a god, whereas Mahayana worships Buddha.
Tripitaka belongs to Buddhism, while Agamas belong to Jainism. Mixing them up is a common mistake.
Digambara monks practice nudity, while Svetambara monks wear clothes. Reversing this can lead to errors in exams.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Represents Vinaya, Sutta, and Abhidhamma Pitaka.
Hinayana treats Buddha as a human, while Mahayana treats him as divine.
Helps remember the key difference between the two Jain sects.

exam_strategy_tips: If the question mentions 'Ashoka' and 'spread', the answer is likely Buddhism.
In sect-based questions, always identify the key differences before answering.
